claims.claim_text: Dozens of people have been killed across the region in clashes between security officials and protesters from the group Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) in the last two months.
claims.subject: protests and clashes in Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: This region is home to about 4.5 million people and currently has elections taking place.
claims.subject: the region of Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: Dr Anwar's clinic has treated around 50 to 60 critically injured patients since 27 July, including 15 to 20 with gunshot wounds.
claims.subject: Dr Anwar's makeshift clinic

claims.claim_text: Protesters are scared to go to the main hospital because they fear they will be arrested or shot.
claims.subject: protesters in Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: The authorities have said that the claim protesters fear being arrested or shot at hospital is inaccurate.
claims.subject: authorities in Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: Most of those killed or seriously injured are young people between about 15-16 years old and 32-35 years old, with very few patients over the age of 40.
claims.subject: casualties at the protests

claims.claim_text: Protesters from the JAAC say the demonstrations are about their rights, including affordable flour, electricity prices, education, and health care.
claims.subject: Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) protesters

claims.claim_text: An agreement signed with the Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir governments in October was meant to help address protesters' concerns, but the JAAC says it has not been implemented.
claims.subject: agreement between Pakistan, Pakistan-administered Kashmir governments and JAAC

claims.claim_text: The local government says the JAAC group is armed and that the protests are about disrupting the ongoing polls.
claims.subject: local government in Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: The local government is not willing to let the protesters march to the regional capital, Muzaffarabad.
claims.subject: local government in Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: The JAAC was banned in June and labeled foreign-funded terrorists by the government.
claims.subject: Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC)

claims.claim_text: The JAAC rejects being characterized as terrorists, says they are peaceful, and claims they are funded from the Pakistan-administered Kashmir community abroad but not sponsored by India.
claims.subject: Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC)

claims.claim_text: JAAC says they are victims and Pakistan's security forces have been firing on them rather than them initiating violence.
claims.subject: Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and Pakistan's security forces

claims.claim_text: The internet is cut and roads are blocked or guarded in Rawalakot, making it difficult to get information about the situation.
claims.subject: access to information in Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Multiple families in the city say they lost loved ones who were shot at the protests.
claims.subject: families in Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Asma said she was at the protest when she heard her only son had been shot.
claims.subject: Asma

claims.claim_text: Salman lost his brother in the protests.
claims.subject: Salman

claims.claim_text: Ayub, a retired armed forces member, lost his son and blames the Pakistan-administered Kashmir government for calling in paramilitary forces.
claims.subject: Ayub

claims.claim_text: The government of Pakistan-administered Kashmir says it rejects the allegation that security forces fired indiscriminately upon peaceful protesters and says law enforcement acted against individuals involved in attacks and threats.
claims.subject: government of Pakistan-administered Kashmir

claims.claim_text: The BBC witnessed food shortages in Rawalakot with many protesters sharing what they had and most shops closed.
claims.subject: food situation in Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Some roads into Rawalakot have been blocked by felled trees, which the authorities say were placed by the JAAC.
claims.subject: road blockades around Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Other entry points to Rawalakot have security checkpoints.
claims.subject: entry points to Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Pakistan-administered Kashmir's government said it is false to suggest they are preventing food or medical supplies from entering Rawalakot, saying they are facilitating the entry of such supplies.
claims.subject: Pakistan-administered Kashmir's government

claims.claim_text: Authorities have repeatedly said that the JAAC are a violent group and have shared drone footage showing what they claim are JAAC members carrying guns on rooftops.
claims.subject: authorities' claims about JAAC

claims.claim_text: Police officials have displayed guns allegedly taken from JAAC members and reported injuries and deaths of security officials, including that one man under interrogation said he was promised a reward for every paramilitary officer killed.
claims.subject: police officials

claims.claim_text: Umar Nazir, a JAAC core committee member, denies the allegation about the reward for paramilitary officer killings but acknowledges some deaths of security officials.
claims.subject: Umar Nazir

claims.claim_text: Umar Nazir believes that certain elements infiltrated the JAAC ranks and may have carried out violent actions to justify authorities' narratives, but he provides no evidence.
claims.subject: Umar Nazir

claims.claim_text: Authorities say the JAAC have engaged in a campaign of disinformation against them, especially on social media.
claims.subject: authorities

claims.claim_text: At JAAC protests the BBC attended, no sign of weaponry or shooting was seen, although overnight repeated gunshots were heard with unclear origin.
claims.subject: BBC observations at JAAC protests

claims.claim_text: The atmosphere in Rawalakot during the protests is tense and uncertain, with unclear prospects for escalation.
claims.subject: current atmosphere in Rawalakot

claims.claim_text: Umar Nazir said the JAAC group is willing to talk and that more protests are planned for now.
claims.subject: Umar Nazir and JAAC plans
